Title: (NIKOLE HANNAH JONES CURATED) A Letter to Black Women in a Country that Doesn't Love Us
Description: Shortly after the election where a white nationalist president defeated the nation's first Black woman Democratic presidential nominee, memes flew across the internet of Black women sipping wine while the nation burned down. The memes felt cathartic -- we had voted against Trump at the highest rates of all groups. But we also knew it would never happen. Black women understand more than anyone the costs of sitting it out, and yet we are so weary of being asked again and again to save this country from itself. This dynamic panel of some of our most beloved and searing public voices will speak to the heartache and resilience of being a Black woman in a country that doesn't love us.

Title: The Essence Cookoff: Reimagining Shrimp & Grits Curated by Chef Nina Compton
Description:
Theme: Reimagining shrimp & grits. Two competing chefs face three judges.

Kick off the ESSENCE Food & Wine experience with an exciting culinary showdown hosted and curated by acclaimed chef, restaurateur, and James Beard Award winner Nina Compton. In this high-energy competition, two talented chefs will put their own spin on one of the South's most beloved dishes: shrimp and grits. Drawing inspiration from New Orleans, the Caribbean, and the broader African diaspora, each chef will reimagine the classic using bold flavors, innovative techniques, and personal storytelling. As the competition heats up, a panel of judges will evaluate each creation based on taste, creativity, presentation, and cultural connection before crowning a winner. 
Blending food, culture, and friendly competition, this lively opening session sets the tone for a weekend celebrating the flavors, traditions, and culinary excellence of Black communities around the world.

Title: Taste of the Diaspora
Description: Food and drink tell the story of who we are, where we've been, and how cultures remain connected across generations and continents. Join us as we explore the rich culinary and beverage traditions of the African diaspora. From Africa to the Caribbean and the American South, this engaging discussion will examine how migration, tradition, entrepreneurship, and innovation continue to shape some of the world's most beloved foods and spirits. Through personal stories, cultural influences, and insights from both the kitchen and behind the bottle, these trailblazers will celebrate the flavors, heritage, and shared experiences that unite communities around the table.

Title: NOLA Kitchen Confidential Curated by Chef Nina Compton
Description:
NOLA chefs in conversation about the city's kitchen culture. 
Step inside the heart of New Orleans' culinary scene with curator and acclaimed chef Nina Compton and celebrated chef Kenneth Temple for an unfiltered conversation about the culture, creativity, and traditions that make the city one of the world's most influential food destinations. From neighborhood kitchens and family recipes to the evolution of modern Creole and Southern cuisine, this session explores the stories, people, and flavors that continue to define New Orleans. Expect candid insights, personal experiences, and a deep dive into the passion, resilience, and community that fuel the city's vibrant food culture.

Title: The ESSENCE Cook-Off: New Orleans Style Okra Showdown Curated by Chef Nina Compton
Description:
Caribbean chefs showcase okra. Afro-Caribbean theme tying NOLA to the diaspora. A staple of New Orleans kitchens and a beloved ingredient throughout the African diaspora, okra takes center stage in this spirited culinary competition curated by Chef Nina Compton. Three talented chefs with roots in the Caribbean and New Orleans will go head-to-head, each creating an original dish that showcases the versatility, flavor, and cultural significance of this iconic ingredient.
Drawing inspiration from Creole, Caribbean, and Southern traditions, competitors will put their own spin on okra while a panel of three esteemed judges evaluates each dish on taste, creativity, technique, and presentation. Who will rise to the occasion and earn the title of ESSENCE Cook-Off Champion?
Filled with bold flavors, friendly rivalry, and plenty of culinary surprises, this high-energy showdown celebrates the rich food traditions that connect New Orleans to the wider African diaspora.

From creating distinctive products to navigating the challenges and opportunities of the brewing and spirits industries, this conversation explores what it means to break barriers, build brands, and create lasting impact. Title: Front of House Femmes OR At Your Service: Celebrating Black Women in Hospitality Curated by Chef Nina Compton
Description:
NOLA hospitality intergenerational panel. Behind every unforgettable dining experience is a hospitality professional who knows how to make guests feel welcome, valued, and at home. In this inspiring intergenerational conversation, New Orleans hospitality leaders Arkesha Baquet of Lil Dizzy's Cafe, Effie of Dakar NOLA, and Zoe Chase, fifth-generation steward of the legendary Dooky Chase's Restaurant, come together to discuss the art of hospitality, preserving family legacies, and creating spaces where culture and community thrive.
Spanning generations and perspectives, this conversation explores the vital role Black women play in shaping New Orleans' hospitality industry while honoring the traditions, resilience, and excellence that continue to define the city's dining culture. From family-owned institutions to modern culinary destinations, these women are carrying forward a legacy of service while helping to shape the future of hospitality.

The suits. The chanting. The call-and-response that fills a room and reminds you exactly where you are. As intricate beadwork catches the light and a brass band carries the energy forward, the Essence main stage comes alive in a celebration that is loud, intentional, and deeply rooted in the culture of this city.
This is how we open. This is how we begin.

Together, they will reflect on the enduring impact of their fathers' work, the responsibility of carrying forward those legacies, and how they have forged their own paths as leaders, advocates, and changemakers. Through personal stories and candid reflections, Dr. King and Dr. Shabazz will discuss navigating racial injustice, division, and uncertainty while remaining grounded in faith, purpose, hope, and action.

Timely, inspiring, and deeply relevant, this historic conversation explores leadership, resilience, and the ongoing pursuit of justice while challenging us to consider how we honor the past, lead in the present, and empower the next generation to create meaningful change.

Title: Declaration of Independence Engagement
Description:
History is being stripped from our classrooms and libraries. As we embark on the 250 anniversary of the United States learn the real history and then hear from the creators and supporters.  

Declarations: Black Americans and the Revolutionary War is a film commemorating America's 250th, from an untold vantage: Black people who fought for the actualization of the Declaration of Independence without assurance it would free them from the bonds of slavery. The film, created by award-winning director Stacey Holman, features some of the nation’s foremost scholars, and it will include groundbreaking use of AI animation programmed with original portraiture. This work will bring exciting energy, vibrant colors, and a modern viewpoint to untold, undiscovered stories that are a crucial part of the history of our country.

Title: Health Care Under Attack: What You Need to Know Now
Description:
New health care laws and policy changes are reshaping who can access critical services, coverage, and resources. As eligibility requirements shift, millions of people may be affected, many without fully understanding what is changing or what options remain available to them.
This session will help attendees understand the latest changes to health care access, what they may mean for individuals, families, and communities, and how to navigate available tools, services, and resources. From eligibility and enrollment to prevention, care coordination, and community-based support, this conversation will offer practical guidance on how people can protect their health in a rapidly changing environment.

Title: The State of the Workforce for Black Women
Description:
Black women are among the most educated groups in the United States and have long been a driving force of the economy. Yet many Black women are finding themselves at a crossroads. Some are choosing to leave workplaces that have become increasingly toxic, isolating, or hostile. Others are being pushed out of jobs and leadership pipelines—not because of performance or qualifications, but because of persistent discrimination and the erosion of initiatives designed to expand opportunity and accountability.
As companies retreat from diversity, equity, and inclusion commitments, many Black women are experiencing the consequences firsthand. The result is not only a workforce challenge, but an economic one—with implications for income, wealth building, entrepreneurship, leadership representation, and family stability.
This session will examine the realities facing Black women in today’s workforce, the impact of anti-DEI policies and practices, and what it will take to create workplaces where Black women can thrive, lead, and build lasting economic security. From corporate leadership and entrepreneurship to policy solutions and power building, the conversation will explore a path forward at a pivotal moment for Black women and the future of work.

Title: The Power of Black Philanthropy: Investing in Our Future
Description:
For generations, Black communities have practiced philanthropy—pooling resources, supporting institutions, and investing in collective progress even when excluded from traditional sources of wealth and capital. Today, as many organizations face funding challenges and longstanding commitments to equity come under attack, the role of Black philanthropy has never been more important.
This session will explore how philanthropy can be leveraged not only to address immediate needs, but also to build long-term power, opportunity, and economic mobility. From individual giving and family philanthropy to corporate investments, foundations, and community-led funding models, the conversation will examine how strategic investments can strengthen institutions, support innovation, advance justice, and help shape a more equitable future.
At a moment when many are asking what comes next, this discussion will focus on the unique role Black philanthropy can play in sustaining communities, protecting progress, and investing in the next generation of leaders and change makers.

Title: All Roads Lead to the South: Black Voters Matter - How We Fight for Our Rights, Protect Our People, and Nation Build!!!
Description:
Following the Supreme Courts' gutting of the Voting Rights Act, Black political power has been under attack. Although this has been most noticeable in the South, our history has shown what happens in the South affects all of us. 
The South has been a blueprint for resilience, creativity, community, and power. As the country finishes its first 250 years, Black communities are radically reimagining the nation we are building for the next 250.
